niche_preference_profile: Prefers interfaces that feel structured, intentional, and visually resolved: clear hierarchy, modular grouping, strong scanability, and low clutter. They often like calm, modern, premium-looking product UIs with restrained chrome, subtle progress treatment, rounded components, and concise copy. They also repeatedly value screens that feel complete and functional rather than sparse or placeholder-like. In some contexts they strongly respond to dramatic, high-contrast, urgent alert styling and to immersive dark/glassy aesthetics, but those signals are not fully consistent across all tasks.

criteria.description: Prefers strong top-down hierarchy with prominent headings, clearly separated sections, and orderly progression of content.
Prefers quieter screens with fewer competing elements, less decorative interruption, and restrained use of extra UI chrome.
Prefers content broken into distinct, digestible modules or sections rather than mixed flows or loosely grouped content.
Prefers layouts that are easy to scan quickly through short rows, repeated patterns, concise blocks, and predictable structure.
Prefers screens that feel fully populated, finished, and operational rather than sparse, empty, or placeholder-like.
Prefers repeated component patterns and cohesive visual rhythm, with consistent cards, rows, separators, and control treatments.
Prefers a composed, modern, premium product feel over generic template styling, overly promotional treatment, or casual visual tone.
Prefers shorter, tighter, more direct wording over verbose explanatory text.
Prefers layouts with intentional breathing room and balanced spacing that separate modules cleanly without feeling empty.
Prefers navigation and progress cues that are integrated cleanly into the layout and do not compete heavily with content.
Prefers interfaces where primary actions and available controls are obvious, legible, and decisively signaled.
Prefers soft rounded cards, buttons, and containers that feel contemporary and polished.
Prefers explicit section labels, named modules, and visible structural scaffolding that clarifies what each area contains.
Prefers onboarding that feels practical, product-like, and utility-focused rather than promotional, decorative, or lifestyle-led.
Prefers meaningful layering or surface separation when it improves context, depth, and visual organization rather than feeling detached or flat.
Prefers color used purposefully to communicate meaning, differentiate actions, or support scanning rather than as generic decoration.
